blocks.text:
Today you visit the Chimborazo reserve and the Ingapirca archaeological complex.

The reserve was established in 1987.

One of its aims is to restore populations of Andean camelids: llamas, alpacas and vicuñas.

Vicuñas were brought here from Peru and Chile.

The reserve’s main natural landmark is the Chimborazo volcano, Ecuador’s highest mountain.

It rises to more than 6,000 m.

The Carihuairazo volcano is nearby.

During the excursion, you can see high-altitude páramo grasslands and vicuñas, and visit viewpoints and a mountain refuge.

A packed lunch is included.

From Chimborazo, you continue to the ruins of Ingapirca.

This is Ecuador’s largest and most important Inca archaeological complex.

The complex dates to the 15th and 16th centuries.

One of its most distinctive structures is the elliptical Temple of the Sun.

It measures about 37 m long and 12 m wide.

The Cañari and Inca peoples used it for ceremonies and rituals.

You also visit Pilaloma, one of the oldest sections of the complex, which consists of rectangular rooms.

The ruins are open to visitors from Wednesday to Sunday.

On other days, you view the complex from outside the fence.

After the excursion, you travel to Cuenca.

The evening is free.

You stay at the 4-star El Dorado.

Breakfast and a packed lunch are included.
White church tower above the tiled rooftops of Cuenca, with green mountains in the background, Ecuador
